title: Jaipur D2C accessories brand killed 27 of 45 influencers using geo-holdout, not the Shopify dashboard — ROAS recovered 3.4 → 3.9
content: A Jaipur D2C accessories brand (silver-toned jewellery, sunglasses; ~₹1.1cr/month revenue) was spending ₹6.2L/month across 45 nano and micro Instagram creators. Shopify's last-click dashboard credited influencers with just 9% of sales and handed the rest to Meta and Google, so the founder was ready to axe the entire influencer line. Before cutting, we ran two checks. First, a unique WhatsApp keyword ('GLOW') per creator tier plus creator-specific landing pages. Second, a 3-week geo holdout pausing all influencers in Pune and Ahmedabad. The story flipped: 'GLOW' WhatsApp enquiries plus coded landing pages traced 22% of orders to creators, and in the paused cities Meta CPMs rose 31% while blended ROAS fell 3.4 → 2.6 — influencers were warming audiences Meta then closed and claimed. But the holdout also exposed that ~60% of the 45 creators drove zero incremental lift. We cut those 27 dead-weight creators, redirected ₹2.5L into 8 proven ones plus a WhatsApp retargeting flow, and added UTM-tagged Amazon.in coupon codes. Within 6 weeks blended ROAS recovered to 3.9 and true influencer-attributed revenue settled at 26%.
lesson: Last-click systematically undercredits top-of-funnel influencers because Meta and Google harvest the demand creators seed — judge influencer ROI on a platform dashboard and you will defund your cheapest demand source. Before cutting, prove incrementality with a geo holdout and unique-code attribution (WhatsApp keywords, creator landing pages, UTM coupon codes). The real decision is almost never 'influencers: yes or no' — it's 'which ~30% of creators drive incremental lift, and where does the other 70%'s budget belong'.
